target_offset_note:
SYSTEMATIC TARGET CORRECTION in link_base metres, applied to EVERY grounded target by bringup/approach_target.py. NOT a per-target nudge and not scene-specific.

HOW IT WAS MEASURED (2026-09-01, elevator car): presses of the star-1 button completed all six approach steps without fault but landed low and left. Corrections were applied one at a time against operator observation -- +20 mm up, +20 mm more, 5 mm right, 10 mm right and 1 mm deeper, 5 mm right and 3 mm deeper, then 1 mm back -- converging on CONTACT at [0.003, -0.020, 0.040].

WHY IT IS CALIBRATION AND NOT A FUDGE. The same offset was then applied UNCHANGED to the ADA door plate, a different target on a different wall at a different pose, and that press landed MORE CENTRED than it had without it. A correction that improves two unrelated targets is a property of the rig, not of a scene. The hand-eye solve itself is sound (2.96 mm RMS, worst 8.2 mm, 10 pairs, 63.8 deg rotation spread) -- what this captures is a small systematic error downstream of it that the 120 mm ADA plate tolerated for weeks and the 25 mm elevator buttons exposed immediately. Note the correction is almost entirely lateral and vertical, with only 3 mm along the approach axis: that shape is a camera-to-arm offset, NOT a depth-lift bias, which was my first hypothesis and was wrong.

WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE IT: re-running the hand-eye solve, remounting the camera or the arm, or changing the tool. Re-measure against BOTH a large target and a small one -- a large plate alone cannot see an error this size.
